newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian shares end last week slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian shares end last week slightly lower.

text.p: Shares on the Saudi Arabian stock exchange ended last week slightly softer in trade focused on the services sector, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index was fractionally weaker at 142.24 points in the week to Thursday from a previous 142.55 points.

BFA said 4.29 million shares worth 780.18 million riyals ($208 million) changed hands in the week in 7,168 transactions. The previous week, 4.12 million shares worth 851.42 million riyals were traded.
Of the 60 companies dealt, share prices of 20 rose, 34 fell and six were unchanged, BFA said.
The services sector dominated trade, accounting for 26 percent of total turnover. The cement and banking sectors followed, with 23 percent each.

Electricity firms did well in the week, with SCECO-Southern leading the pack with an over 19 percent gain to 74 riyals from 62 riyals a week earlier. SCECO-Eastern was six percent stronger at 85 riyals and SCECO-Western added two riyals to 77.
SCECO-Central was one riyal firmer at 81.
The biggest loser in the week was Al-Mawashi al-Mukairish 50 percent, which fell to 43 riyals from 60 the previous week.
